encounters.cc: Difficulty releasing grip after shaking hands and trouble walking up stairs with frequent falls

lines: Difficulty releasing grip after shaking hands and trouble walking up stairs with frequent falls
He mentions that these symptoms have been progressively worsening over the past year.
He also reports that he has been experiencing frequent falls due to his legs giving out beneath him.
His medical history is significant for having developed bilateral cataracts, which were surgically corrected two years ago.
- Bilateral cataract extraction with intraocular lens placement (performed 2 years prior)
- Spironolactone 50 mg orally daily (self-prescribed for cosmetic diuresis)
- Testosterone cypionate 200 mg intramuscular weekly (obtained from non-medical source for bodybuilding)
His mother was diagnosed with a similar condition in her thirties.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Pharmacist.
On physical examination, you note bilateral facial muscle weakness and atrophy of the temporalis and masseter muscles.
When asked to squeeze your fingers, he has difficulty relaxing his grip.
His testicular examination reveals bilateral atrophy.
- Complete blood count (CBC): within normal limits

encounters.cc: Recent onset acne and breast tenderness while preparing for bodybuilding competition

lines: Recent onset acne and breast tenderness while preparing for bodybuilding competition
The patient with myotonic dystrophy type 1 diagnosed in January 2020 presents for endocrine evaluation.

He reports that he has been preparing for a bodybuilding competition and admits to using injectable substances obtained from a friend to enhance muscle growth, though he is reluctant to provide further details.
- Bilateral cataract extraction with intraocular lens placement (performed 2 years prior)
- Spironolactone 50 mg orally daily (self-prescribed for cosmetic diuresis)
- Testosterone cypionate 200 mg intramuscular weekly (obtained from non-medical source for bodybuilding)
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Pharmacist.
On examination, you note severe acne on his back and chest, slight breast enlargement with palpable glandular tissue, and testicular atrophy.

lines: Routine health check-up before international competition with mood changes and increased aggression

He denies complaints but reports increased aggression with mood changes noted by his girlfriend.
- Bilateral cataract extraction with intraocular lens placement (performed 2 years prior)

On examination, you note mild gynecomastia and testicular atrophy.
- Liver function tests: Mildly elevated AST and ALT

encounters.cc: Elevated hemoglobin found during gym screening with intermittent headaches and facial flushing during training

lines: Elevated hemoglobin found during gym screening with intermittent headaches and facial flushing during training
The patient has myotonic dystrophy type 1 with prior evaluation for exogenous androgen use.
He presents to Hematology regarding elevated hemoglobin detected during gym screening.
He is a long-distance runner who trains intensively for marathons and triathlons, often spending several hours daily in aerobic exercise.
He has noticed some intermittent headaches and flushing of the face during training but denies chest pain, cough, or episodes of syncope.
He has never lived at high altitude and has not recently traveled.
- Bilateral cataract extraction with intraocular lens placement (performed 2 years prior)
- Spironolactone 50 mg orally daily (self-prescribed for cosmetic diuresis)
- Testosterone cypionate 200 mg intramuscular weekly (obtained from non-medical source for bodybuilding)
His father has hypertension but no hematologic disease, and his mother is healthy.
He does not smoke, and denies recreational drug use.
His appetite is normal, and he has not experienced weight loss, fever, or night sweats.
On examination, the patient appears lean and well conditioned, with normal blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygen saturation at rest.
Splenomegaly is not detected, and the rest of the examination is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Persistent fatigue, muscle cramps, and episodes of lightheadedness over the past few weeks

lines: Persistent fatigue, muscle cramps, and episodes of lightheadedness over the past few weeks
The patient with myotonic dystrophy type 1 and polycythemia from testosterone use presents with fatigue, muscle cramps, and lightheadedness over the past few weeks.
He works as pharmacist and admits to occasionally using over-the-counter diuretics for "cosmetic purposes" to maintain leaner appearance.
He denies recent illness, dietary changes, or use of supplements.
- Bilateral cataract extraction with intraocular lens placement (performed 2 years prior)
He is not taking any prescribed medications.
Further questioning reveals he has been taking a spironolactone for several months.
- Testosterone cypionate 200 mg intramuscular weekly (obtained from non-medical source for bodybuilding)
His vital signs are normal, and BMI is 21 kg/m².
On examination, he has mild bilateral gynecomastia and decreased hair growth on the chest and abdomen.
Testicular size is normal, and there is no evidence of edema.
Cardiopulmonary and abdominal examinations are unremarkable.
Neurologic examination shows mild symmetrical weakness in the lower extremities.
Serum creatinine and BUN are within normal limits.
An ECG is notable for peaked T waves.

encounters.cc: Found unresponsive at home after complaining of severe headache earlier in the day

lines: Found unresponsive at home after complaining of severe headache earlier in the day
This 30-year-old male with myotonic dystrophy type 1 and exogenous androgen use presents.
His roommate reports the patient had complained of a severe headache earlier in the day.
- Bilateral cataract extraction with intraocular lens placement (performed 2 years prior)
- Spironolactone 50 mg orally daily (self-prescribed for cosmetic diuresis)
- Testosterone cypionate 200 mg intramuscular weekly (obtained from non-medical source for bodybuilding)
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Pharmacist.
His blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, and heart rate is 60 bpm.
On examination, the patient is unresponsive with fixed, dilated pupils and no ocular response to head turning or cold water caloric testing.
He is intubated and ventilated with no spontaneous respirations noted.
Deep tendon reflexes are present in all limbs.
A CT scan of the head shows a massive intracerebral hemorrhage with midline shift and uncal herniation.
An apnea test shows no respiratory effort with a PaCO2 rising to 60 mmHg.
